DRS: Drag Reduction System — opens rear wing on straights for more speed. Abolished in 2026, replaced by active aero.
activeAero: 2026 innovation — wings automatically adjust angle every corner and straight. Always optimizing.
undercut: Pitting before your rival to gain track position via fresher, faster tyres
overcut: Staying out longer than your rival, hoping your fresher tyres later make the difference
blistering: Tyres overheating causing surface chunks to break off — destroys lap times
graining: Cold tyre surface tearing before it warms up — common in cool conditions
MGUK: Motor Generator Unit Kinetic — harvests energy from braking, deploys on acceleration. 350kW in 2026.
MGUH: Motor Generator Unit Heat — harvested turbo energy. Completely removed in 2026.
groundEffect: Aerodynamic downforce generated from the car's floor — retained in 2026
porpoising: Bouncing effect from ground effect cars at high speed — plagued 2022 cars
parcFerme: After qualifying, cars are locked — no setup changes allowed before race
VSC: Virtual Safety Car — all drivers must maintain delta time, no overtaking. Less disruptive than full SC.
SC: Safety Car — all cars must follow behind, no overtaking. Deployed for accidents or dangerous conditions.
pitWindow: The optimal lap range to pit based on tyre degradation and track position
stacking: When a team pits both cars in the same lap — risky but sometimes necessary
freeStop: When a safety car allows a driver to pit without losing track position — massive strategic advantage
parc ferme: Controlled environment after qualifying — teams cannot change car setup
delta: The time difference between a driver and the VSC target time they must maintain
marbles: Rubber debris that builds up off the racing line — very slippery, dangerous to drive on
dirty air: Turbulent air behind a car that reduces downforce for following cars — 2026 regs aim to reduce this
rake: The angle of the car from front to back — affects aerodynamic balance
downforce: Aerodynamic force pushing car into track — more downforce = more grip = faster corners
oversteer: Rear of car slides out in corners — exciting to watch, difficult to manage
understeer: Front of car pushes wide in corners — safer but slower
ERS: Energy Recovery System — collective term for MGU-K and MGU-H (MGU-H removed 2026)
deployment: When and how a driver uses their electric power — critical strategy in 2026
fuel load: Amount of fuel in car — heavier at start, lighter as race progresses
tyre compound: Soft (red) = fastest but fragile. Medium (yellow) = balanced. Hard (white) = durable but slow. Inter (green) = light rain. Wet (blue) = heavy rain.
